technique: Reads as a 3D-rendered puppet built to emulate a felt/needle-felted stop-motion look rather than genuine handmade stop-motion. However, the coffee steam curls in continuous, fluid, non-jittery arcs across every frame, the camera is perfectly locked/steady with no set-jitter or fingerprint artifacts typical of tabletop stop-motion, and the shallow-DOF traffic bokeh behind the windshield looks like a rendered/composited backdrop rather than a miniature set shot with a macro lens. This is most consistent with CG (or AI-generated) animation applying a faux-stop-motion material/shader, not frame-by-frame physical puppet animation. Flagging real uncertainty here since only 12 sparse keyframes are available and no true single-frame-advance evidence (e.g. held double-frames) can be confirmed.

idle_motion_notes: The single consistently animated ambient element is steam rising from the coffee cup, which curls into a visibly different, continuously varying shape in nearly every sampled frame -- the only piece of secondary/idle motion in an otherwise static tableau. Background traffic (taillights, parked-looking cars, foggy skyline) shows no visible change across the wide-shot frames, reading as a static or near-static backdrop rather than continuously simulated traffic.
frame_rate_feel: Metadata reports 30fps, but the perceived cadence is far choppier/sparser than that: across seven sampled wide-shot frames spanning a large portion of the clip's ~11.6s runtime, character poses are essentially unchanged, implying the animators are holding poses for extended spans (consistent with animating well below 30fps, e.g. 2s/lower-frame-rate holds) while only the steam sim reads as continuously smooth. The result is a deliberate 'mostly-still diorama with one animated flourish' feel rather than fluid full-frame-rate character motion, punctuated by a slower-but-still-incremental facial turn in the closing close-up shot.
overall_animation_style_notes: Moody, desaturated blue-grey commute lighting with glowing red taillight bokeh and heavy atmospheric fog reads as a cinematic live-action lens language (shallow depth of field, rack focus onto the driver's face) layered onto a felt-textured character design -- an exaggerated long conical nose, blocky torso, visible wool/fiber grain, and simple painted-on facial features (flat eyebrow shapes, dot pupils).
